text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German bonds were closed on Monday for a market hoilday. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.54, down 0.33 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts drifted lower after April PSDR came in at 36 million stg compared with a forecast 1.7 billion stg deficit. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-14/32, down 11/32 from Friday's settlement price.
FRANCE - French bonds were closed on Monday for a market holiday.

ITALY - Bonds and futures swung higher on optimism over the chances of an official rate cut once preliminary inflation data have been released this week. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.84, up 0.69 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were nearly unchanged in mid-morning trade. Trading was quiet as market awaits Fed's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) monetary policy meeting on Tuesday. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-01/32, up 02/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.91 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed higher on Monday on dealer short-covering, market sources said. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.51, up 0.13 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was at a standstill on Monday morning with most centres on continental Europe closed for a holiday. The meeting of the policy-making U.S. Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday means the delayed start to the week will likely be extended, dealers said.
Among limited related activity, Daily Mail and General Trust Plc offered to buy back the 48 million stg outstanding on its 5.75 percent 2003 bond exchangeable into Reuters shares.
Daily Mail will issue a new bond due 2004 which will be exchangeable into Reuters shares. J.P. Morgan Securities will arrange/lead manage the two separate Daily Mail transactions.
The repurchase price of the 2003 bonds will be at an indicated 6-8 percent premium over the market price.
